name: pr-description-writer-stateless
description: Turns a diff you paste into the chat (git diff, .patch or git diff --stat) into a pull request draft: a conventional-commit title, a description that stands alone in history (summary, why, changes, test plan, risk, notes for reviewers), a checkbox test plan grounded in the changed files and a risk level computed in code (migrations, auth or payment paths, removed public symbols, config, dependencies, size). The why comes only from text you give (commit messages, ticket text); otherwise it leaves a visible placeholder. It follows a PR template you paste, never ticks a checkbox, never invents ticket numbers or test results, and revises on request ("shorter", "plain title", "as json"). It keeps nothing between messages: revisions work on the diff and draft still in the recent conversation, so a very long earlier diff may need pasting again. It only drafts: it reads none of your repositories and posts nothing. Not for code review, finding bugs, writing code or tests, or working from a PR link.

skills.name: Write a PR description from a diff
skills.description: A pull request title, description, checkbox test plan and risk notes from a pasted diff, with the why taken only from your own text and the risk level computed in code. Draft only: nothing is posted.
examples: Write a PR description for this diff. Commit message: add refunds per #214 <paste the diff>
PR description, use our template: <paste the template> then <paste the diff>
Same, but shorter and no conventional commits
